name: Oying
ingredients: Fresh seasonal leafy greens (like mustard greens or pumpkin leaves)
Optional: Smoked pork or dried fish (for non-veg variant)
instructions: 1. Wash and chop the leafy greens into medium-sized pieces.
2. Slice the fresh bamboo shoot into thin strips.
3. In a large pot, bring a moderate amount of water to a boil.
4. Add the bamboo shoots and chopped ginger to the boiling water.
5. Once the bamboo shoots are tender, add the leafy greens and green chilies.
6. Season with salt to taste and simmer until the vegetables are cooked but still retain their vibrant color.
7. Serve hot, traditionally paired with steamed red rice.
description: Oying is a quintessential staple of the Adi community in Arunachal Pradesh. It represents the indigenous culinary philosophy of using locally foraged ingredients, emphasizing health and simplicity. It is often served as a comforting daily accompaniment to rice, reflecting the symbiotic relationship between the forest and the tribal kitchen.
